the mGlu8 ATD is a highly conserved protein domain that has a similar structure and binding mode as other published mGlu ATDs.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the mGlu8 ATD structure provides the first structural evidence that explains the molecular basis for the functional potency and selectivities of L-AP3 and L-AP5, and the first evidence that the distal phosphate group contributes to L-AP4 binding and functional potency.
the mGlu8 ATD has a unique binding pocket for L-AP and L-glu, which may be a key determinant for the group selectivity of L-AP.

the mGlu8 ATD structure in complex with the L-AP4 provides the molecular basis for the group III mGmu receptor agonist functional potency and selectivities, and also provides the structural foundation for the rational design of more potent and selective group III mGm receptor agonists.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mGlu ATDs have evolved to accommodate the different chemical properties of the natural ligand L-glu and the synthetic ligand L-AP4 in order to achieve group III functional selectivity.
the ATD is a critical structural determinant for the group III functional potency and selectivities of mGlu agonists.

the ATDs of the group III receptors are more flexible in comparison with those of other mGlu subgroups and the ATDs of group III receptors are likely to be more tolerant to the presence of the distal phosphonate moiety in comparison with other mGlu ATDs.
